Blenheim, Hanover: reconstruction of Alexander Bustamante’s birthplace in JNHT’s source photograph. It is explicitly a replica, not the intact house from 1884. Photographer and capture date unspecified.

Lacovia tombstone site, St. Elizabeth, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified; this small view cannot independently verify the complete inscription or a heraldic genealogy.

Savanna-la-Mar fort, Westmoreland, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified; surviving coastal masonry does not depict the full proposed fort or its eighteenth-century condition.

Marshall’s Pen great house, Manchester, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified. The image is not a reconstruction of the enslaved village or a guarantee of present tour access.
Jamaican owl downy chick and adult at Marshall’s Pen, Manchester, identified in the source caption as March 2017.

Halse Hall great house, Clarendon, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; the visible two-storey house is not the original single-storey building of Thomas Halse’s lifetime.
Liberty Hall, 76 King Street, Kingston, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified. The restored facade is not a dated photograph of a 1923 meeting.
Fort Charlotte, Lucea, Hanover, in JNHT’s undated source photograph, showing surviving masonry and a gun position. Photographer unspecified; not a reconstruction of the eighteenth-century garrison.

Burchell Memorial Church interior, Montego Bay, St. James, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; it does not show the original sanctuary destroyed during the 1831–1832 conflict.

Good Hope great-house interior, Trelawny, in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified. Furnishings visible in this later view do not establish the room’s eighteenth-century arrangement.
Flat Bridge over the Rio Cobre, St. Catherine, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; this is not a view of the eighteenth-century timber deck.
Old King’s House facade, Spanish Town, St. Catherine, in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified. The surviving facade is not the intact pre-1925 residence.
Ward Theatre, North Parade, Kingston, in JNHT’s undated exterior photograph. Photographer unspecified. This is the 1912 theatre’s later appearance, not an image of its destroyed predecessor.
Cinchona Botanical Garden, St. Andrew: terraces, planting and buildings in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; not a guarantee of present garden or road conditions.
Mona great house, St. Andrew, in JNHT’s source photograph. It is a separate estate residence, not the campus chapel or a Gibraltar Camp barrack. Capture date and photographer unspecified.
Archival album page with a photograph of buildings at Gibraltar Camp, Jamaica, dated 1940–1941.
Stokes Hall great-house ruins, St. Thomas, in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; visible walls do not establish the complete original plan.

Morant Point lighthouse, St. Thomas: the tall tower in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified; the photograph does not establish present access or operating characteristics.
Folly Point lighthouse, Portland, in JNHT’s source photograph. This is a nearby, separate landmark, not the Folly mansion. Capture date and photographer unspecified.

Moore Town, Portland: monument and plaque at the site associated with Nanny, in JNHT’s source photograph. Capture date and photographer unspecified. The image is not a reconstruction of an eighteenth-century settlement.
Accompong entrance, St. Elizabeth, in JNHT’s undated later photograph. Photographer unspecified; it is not an image of the eighteenth-century treaty negotiations.
Roxborough site, Manchester, in JNHT’s undated later photograph. The visible roofed structure is not evidence that Norman Manley’s original birth house survives unchanged.
Building identified by JNHT as Claude McKay’s birthplace, Clarendon. Photographer and image date unspecified; this photograph does not establish the building’s present condition.
Kenilworth industrial ruins, Hanover, in JNHT’s later source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified. The walls are not a complete reconstruction of the operating works.

Kendal railway disaster, Manchester, 1957: wrecked carriage and people beside the train in the image published by JNHT. Photographer and exact capture date unspecified; not a present-day visitor scene.
Frome, Westmoreland: an editorial chronology constructed from the 4 May 1938 parliamentary report and NLJ’s Labour Day history. This is a learning graphic, not a period photograph.
Entrance to Bath Botanical Gardens, St. Thomas, in JNHT’s source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified. The gate image does not establish current opening or plant identification.

DeMontevin Lodge on Titchfield Peninsula, Port Antonio, Portland, identified on JNHT’s district page. Photographer and capture date unspecified; the image does not establish current accommodation or interior access.
Devon House, St. Andrew, in the JNHT source photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified. A restored exterior does not show the complete 1881 household.
Kingston Railway Station, Kingston parish. Later exterior photograph published by JNHT; photographer and capture date unspecified. The image does not establish present rail service or public access.
Freedom Monument in Sam Sharpe Square, Montego Bay, St. James. JNHT photograph, capture date and photographer unspecified. This is a later memorial, not the site as it appeared in 1832.
Waterloo House on High Street, Black River, St. Elizabeth. JNHT photograph, photographer and capture date unspecified. This later view does not establish present condition or visitor access.
Seaford Town villa, Westmoreland, identified by JNHT as a former convent. Photographer and capture date unspecified; the image does not establish the building’s original construction date.
Sligoville, St. Catherine: a later street scene published by JNHT, photographer and capture date unspecified. It is not an image of the 1835 purchase.
St. Peter’s Church at Alley, Clarendon. JNHT source photograph, date and photographer unspecified. The building shown is not the original 1671 structure.
Mandeville Court House, Manchester, in the JNHT photograph. Photographer and capture date unspecified; this later exterior is not a picture of the 1817 construction.
Maidstone entrance, Manchester. Photograph published by JNHT; photographer and capture date unspecified. This is a later view of the community, not an image made in 1840.
Identified portrait of Reverend A. A. Barclay, wearing glasses and a clerical collar
An unnamed worker beside a suspended banana bunch, with harvested bunches lined on the ground, Jamaica, 1940
River landscape photographed from Wag Water Bridge, archive dated 1900–1910
Pencar River Bridge and its dirt-road approach with coconut palms, St. Mary, 1890–1895
Front page of Negro World, 31 July 1920, announcing a world convention and a constitution of liberty
Original first page of the Jamaica Independence Act 1962, Chapter 40, showing the 19 July date and section one appointing 6 August
Album page with Old Government House at left and a memorial at right, Spanish Town, 1930–1939
